subject_judgments.rationale: Paris > revolt against the Crown (1789)112 retrieves the practical collapse and constrained recognition after July. Municipal revolution113 retrieves provincial displacement; August Decrees > king's refusal to sanction121 explicitly retrieves his delayed, qualified assent; Louis XVI > relocation to Paris122 retrieves forced assent and confinement; Louis XVI > constitutional role and powers123 retrieves the end of open resistance and deliberately weakened executive. Together these supported routes retrieve every treatment. However, the same royal relocation heading falsely supplies112 as an October Days destination, merging the July conciliatory visit with October confinement. This is a material chronological contradiction to the retained distinction, although122 and the alternative Paris112 path independently supply the correct account. Coverage remains complete, while stance preservation and first lookup are partial because this direct royal route is misleading. Complete treatment recall does not establish complete multi-facet access because realistic first lookup is not fully successful.

The subdivided Constitution of1791 entry retrieves executive weakness and drafting123–124, the three-year ministerial exclusion124, the completed amendments155, amnesty156 and acceptance/contradictory legacy157. Separation of powers119 supplies the explicit constitutional criterion, while Parlements > abolition125 directly retrieves the removal of courts' political/administrative prerogatives and the new institutional separation. Feuillants154 identifies the conservative consolidation after repression, and Feuillants158 directly retrieves the final rejection of their expectation of stable constitutional life. Full119,123–125,154–158 inspected. Franchise155 retrieves both removal of the deputy silver-mark test and the higher secondary-elector threshold after elections; it does not imply simple democratization. The amnesty route156 also retains continued officer departure. All retained distinctions and both facets are available without conflating enduring administrative achievement with political legitimacy. The unsupported franchise123 posting is not credited; its correct124/155 destinations remain separately usable. No new parent-level stance or navigation loss is demonstrated by that wrong-page posting.

National Guard has focused creation, membership, provincial disturbance, martial-law and named journee subdivisions. Creation112–113 and Lafayette command112–113 retrieve institution and difficulty restraining lynchings; tricolour112 preserves the king accepting city colours before Lafayette adds royal white, while the121 posting retrieves the later repudiation of the emblem. Peasant resistance115 directly retrieves why inexperienced militias could not restrain the rural movement, alongside the distrust of troops. Veto120, October Days122 and active citizens124 retrieve the stated contrast between indispensable popular intervention and restricted power. Guard martial law125–126 retrieves absent police machinery, municipal red flags, firing powers, army distrust and unreliable discipline. Membership128 explicitly retrieves uniform costs, active-citizen eligibility, oaths and federations; provincial130 retrieves late intervention and uniformed rioters. Provincial138/143/147 preserves Protestant and Catholic differences, Jales reversal and influence on regular ranks. Guard order and Lafayette command148 retrieves refusal at Saint-Cloud, Varennes151 retrieves mobilization along the flight route, and Guard Champ de Mars154 retrieves repression. These are useful direct topical or named crisis routes to each distinct treatment, not interchangeable mere mentions of guards. All full destination pages read; no claim of uniform politics or socially universal citizenship. Identical repeated C005-S004 requirement is acknowledged as one repeated semantic obligation pending canonical duplicate correction.

Sovereignty118 directly retrieves the opening explanation that binding mandates were abolished on8July, freeing national representatives before the August settlement. National Assembly > assertion of sovereignty and early decrees117 reaches the explicit contrast between original mandates and sweeping August action. The neutral sovereignty heading retains the earlier chronology rather than presenting abolition as an August response. The retained distinction's broader134–135 comparison is separately retrieved through Cahiers > impact on revolutionary policy134 and Reform > revolutionary (1789-1791) > constitutional and administrative135: both specifically concern the relationship between authorized instructions and actual reform, not chance arrival through an unrelated same-page name. Full117,118,134,135 read; all selected routes retain direct useful supported destinations.

Peasant resistance114–115/128 supplies the initial expectations, selective attacks on records and material symbols, forced renunciations, and continuing nonpayment after the legal settlement. August Decrees117 retrieves the failure of redemption. Liberty trees130 expressly retrieves May-tree custom adapted into a supposed year-and-day extinction of rights, organized demands and defence of trees; seigneurial rights130 supplies continued attacks and the legislators' property-based response. Full114–115,117,128,130 read. These dated source destinations preserve the1789–1791 sequence, avoid treating all violence as indiscriminate, and distinguish legal symbolism from actual legislated abolition. All five retained distinctions are accessible without crediting the chronologically partial Great-Fear130 alternative.

Focused Assignats origins133–134 retrieves Extraordinary Fund, national lands, bond-to-currency transformation, compensation and confessional/banking objections. Assembly finance and national debt132 retrieves expanded compensation obligations. Reform135 retrieves unmandated paper money in the summary. Assignats decline285, final collapse286, and controlled economy290 retrieves depreciation, market procurement and retrospective popular memories. Final collapse322–323 reaches emergency levies, failed land bank, plate destruction and successor mandates while preserving their distinct forms. Origins402 and decline/social impact403 retrieves over-issue as main cause, wartime intensification, lost real land proceeds and redistribution against creditors, wages and fixed incomes. Guard against conflating the legal-tender chronology: source134 and265 differ, headings do not assert a single date. All selected source destinations fully read.

Paris > revolt against the Crown112 retrieves continuing hunger and conspiracy fears; municipal revolution113 and Great Fear114 retrieve the different urban and rural material settings. Paris > bread prices and subsistence riots121 explicitly retrieves dry rivers/mills, real shortage, convoy protests and women's action; Flanders Regiment121 supplies the renewed military threat and banquet reports. October Days122 retrieves demands for bread, other participants joining, flour as conciliation and natural/administrative limits to royal relief. Full112–114/121–122 read. The routes do not turn rumours of deliberate starvation into established facts and preserve women's initiating role alongside broader earlier participation. Both retained distinctions and all principal/supporting treatments are available.

Declaration of the Rights of Man > principles118–119 provides the direct first lookup for adoption, natural rights, national sovereignty, general-will law, accountability, legal guarantees and separated powers. The destination explicitly retains public-order qualifications on expression and religion and the enduring manifesto distinct from its constitution. August decrees116–117 retrieves civil, fiscal, corporate, provincial and officeholding privilege, not merely feudal dues. Active citizens and franchise124 exposes unequal political eligibility despite civil equality; taxation > during the Revolution and Privilege131 retrieves the replacement taxes without special exemptions. Property rights132 directly reaches the argument that Church nationalization violates the Declaration, alongside Church property, thus preserving the competing interpretations rather than silently treating appropriation as consistent. All selected full pages were read, all selected complete paths are supported. Each retained distinction and the 118/119/132 facet has a useful topical route without implying later institutional applications were themselves declaration provisions.

National Assembly > financial policy131 and Necker > financial management131 retrieve refusal of bankruptcy and the persistent inherited debt. Patriotic contribution132 directly retrieves the quarter-income levy, unverified declarations and poor yield; national debt132 supplies the debt expansion including compensation. Assignats > origins and land-backing133–134 retrieves the Extraordinary Fund's contribution and land-sale receipts and the repeated expansion driven by deficits and office compensation. Full131–134 read. The financing sequence and failure of patriotic voluntary collection are preserved, rather than reduced to an unexplained failure or a claim that constitutional reform cured the debt.

Peasant resistance114–115/128 directly retrieves expectations, targeted refusal, documentary/material attacks, coercive renunciation and continued use of seigneurial resources. August Decrees117 explicitly credits nonpayment with practical destruction beyond legal redemption. Seigneurial rights130 retrieves liberty-tree assertions, threatened title deeds, selective violence and legislators' refusal to recognize peasants' distinctions. Full114–115/117/128/130 read. The complete routes preserve the independent peasant mechanism and its continuation after the panic. The chronologically partial peasantry > Revolution of1789 > Great Fear/rural unrest130 posting is excluded; the accurate seigneurial-rights130 route independently supplies the later claim.

Active citizens124 and Constitution > franchise124 directly retrieve male/age/tax exclusions, the three-tier active-citizen/elector/deputy structure, silver mark, controversy and reduced suffrage compared with1789. August Decrees116 and Declaration118–119 supply civil/fiscal equality as an explicit contrast, not evidence of voting rights. Sovereignty118, royal veto120, Paris > October Days122 and National Guard > martial law126 retrieve popular assistance followed by representative defiance and coercive control. Departments125 explicitly places active-citizen eligibility in local office. Full116,118–120,122,124–126 read. All five retained distinctions are accessible; no universal-franchise claim is inferred from equal taxation or from active citizenship.

Courtiers112 retrieves the early Artois-associated departures; nobility > emigration123 supplies the distinct post-October wave. Émigrés > noble emigration128 and nobility abolition128 retrieve withdrawal from seats/elections and the1790 abolition of status and symbols. Seigneurial rights130 directly supplies continuing attacks and landlords' dread; nobility > legislative and political activity135 retrieves the important patriotic counterexample alongside dissenters. Full112,123,128,130,135 read. Separate focused entries preserve differing dates, motives and conduct, so neither all nobles nor all émigrés are treated as a homogeneous rejectionist group.

Cahiers > impact on revolutionary policy134 explicitly retrieves the Assembly's claimed mandate versus unrequested institutional changes. Reform135 directly retrieves the interpretation that revolution and unprecedented events produced measures beyond the cahiers, cross-status participation despite damaged interests, and chaotic implementation alongside broad acceptance. Feast of the Federation128/135 supplies the genuine but short-lived consensus and its impending breakup. Full128,134–135 read; the selected headings make no assertion that every change was authorized, society uniformly hostile, or execution orderly. All retained distinctions and coalesced principal/supporting/concluding treatments are available.

Marat and L Ami du Peuple120 retrieve political scrutiny and suspicion, with same quotation continuing121 to innocent-victim qualification. Desmoulins124/126 retrieves democratic journalism and political organization. Church property132 explicitly contains newspaper intervention in the property controversy; Marat134 retrieves pressure in the finance debate. Federation128 supplies separately retained political-song suspicion without treating songs as newspaper evidence. Full required pages and immediate continuations read; all actual locator destinations supported. Semantic access is complete/stance preserved/first lookup succeeds; only retained C005-S042133→132 source metadata binding remains pending.

August Decrees > origins in rural unrest115 supplies the failure of appeals for calm; Breton Club115 identifies the coordinating deputies. The main August Decrees116–117 destinations directly retrieve the tactical recruitment and paired noble interventions, escalating renunciations, private score-settling, later legal restrictions and practical peasant refusal. Declaration > principles118–119 gives equality and office/tax principles, and Departments > administrative reorganization125 supplies the uniform territorial successor. Full115–119/125 inspected. The event heading preserves an escalating process rather than asserting pure altruism or immediate compensated compliance, and all five retained distinctions remain readable through these direct routes.

Feast of the Federation128 directly retrieves the regional rallies, mass constitutional oath, king, religious ceremony and genuine enthusiasm. The same page explicitly turns from optimism in Ça ira to the later threat against aristocrats and alienation, so this is not an unqualified spectacle of universal agreement. Its135 destination supplies the concluding broad consensus and impending breakdown. Full128/135 read. The delivered event heading promises neither unanimity nor permanence, and its two supported destinations preserve both required celebration and qualification; no missing song heading is required to retrieve the stated song contrast within this festival account.

Sovereignty118 retrieves the representatives' autonomous claim; royal veto120 directly retrieves the first flouting of popular opinion, proposed Paris surveillance and direct-action argument. Paris > revolt against the Crown > October Days122 reaches popular enforcement of assent, and National Assembly > relocation to Paris123 explicitly retrieves the central authorities at the mercy of Paris and recurring watchdog intervention. Active citizens124 and National Guard > instrument of order and martial law126 retrieve the political and coercive limits imposed on the same populace. These are specific mechanisms of the required tension, not incidental page intersections. Full118,120,122–124,126 read. The direct contextual routes retain reliance on and fear of popular force without treating the failed August march, October transfer and later martial law as one event.

Danton > Parisian radicalism and section leadership126 and Paris > sections and local government126 specifically retrieve the failed attempt to weaken radical districts, allied newspapers and the political machine's successful transfer into Théâtre-Français. Paris sections126 supplies a further direct route, although its independently reviewed long-list architecture remains a separate exception. The focused Danton route makes realistic first lookup successful and preserves intention versus outcome, ambition and organization. Full126 and eligible129 caption inspected. Paris sections129 literally matches the caption topic but remains an unsupported weak locator, with no map-interior credit;129 is incidental and absent from the scored treatment workset. The receipt's literal-caption scope is satisfied without turning the caption into a substantive fact or claiming local-government detail from it.

Monarchiens119 retrieves Mounier's allies, British-inspired life senate and veto, while royal veto119–120 reaches the free-assent dilemma, suspicion of a privileged upper chamber, its defeat, and the temporary veto compromise despite popular hostility. August Decrees > king's refusal121 and October Days122 retrieve negotiation's failure and coercive assent. Monarchiens123 identifies the later suspicion of Mirabeau's ministerial proposal; separation of powers123 supplies executive limits and two-sitting veto. Full119–123 read. The focused routes distinguish Assembly majorities from wider popular opposition and retain tactical/political motives alongside constitutional theory; all five retained distinctions and treatments are available.

August decrees116 and Declaration119 supply capacity-based equality. Taxation resistance130 and Guard provincial130 retrieve ineffective enforcement; taxation during Revolution131 directly retrieves abolition of old duties, tax farms and direct levies, the three replacements, lack of special privilege and coercion, and the mistaken assumption of willing payment. Assignats origins/Assembly finance134 supplies the actual deficit-revision claim if source correction moves it from132. Fiscal capacity is never equated with political voting rights.

Tax evasion and taxation resistance130 retrieves burned collection facilities, intimidation and expectations of relief; Babeuf and petitioning movement131 directly retrieves his lost employment, organized Picardy campaign and arrest. Taxation131 exposes the irony that the legislators also disliked indirect levies while nonpayment survived reform. Assignats origins/Assembly finance134 retrieves continuing shortfalls and the actual drastic deficit revision. General fiscal resistance is distinguished from Babeuf specific programme; no132 predicate is silently borrowed.

August Decrees117 explicitly distinguishes redeemable dues from outright tithe abolition and credits peasant nonpayment with practical destruction. Peasant resistance128 and seigneurial rights130 directly retrieve continued refusal, threatened title-deeds, detailed redemption rules and enforcement failure. The retained earlier night116 and Church-finance132 qualifications are independently available through August Decrees116 and clergy > abolition of tithes/nationalization132. Full116–117,128,130,132 read. These complementary routes preserve legal property protection versus social noncompliance and the different treatment of clerical revenue; no unsupported conflation is required.

Peasant resistance115 retrieves magistracy impotence. Venality116 and August decrees117 retrieve abolition and compensable office property; separated powers119 supplies principle. Active citizens124 and departments125 retrieve elective public officials and restricted electoral base. Parlements abolition, cassation and jury125 retrieve institutional rupture, new court tiers and unfinished codification; Guard order125–126 and provincial130 retrieve missing police machinery and weak enforcement. Assembly finance/debt132 retrieves actual compensation-expansion predicate, and Assignats origins134 its monetary consequence. Institutional abolition is not confused with real-value compensation, which belongs another parent.

Paris > revolt against the Crown (1789)112 reaches starvation fears, the Bastille governor and Flesselles killings, and displayed heads. Foulon113 directly retrieves the subsequent joint lynching and horrified response. Barnave > revolutionary violence, stance on113 explicitly retrieves the exceptional justification and contrasts it with educated alarm and Lafayette's attempted resignation. The headings do not romanticize or endorse the violence. Full112–113 read; the combined direct Paris and named-victim routes preserve all source treatments and qualifications without needing an invented cross-reference.

Municipal revolution113/126 supplies both the initial property-owning, fear-driven coalition and the later replacement of improvised committees. August Decrees116–117 directly retrieves town/provincial privilege renunciation and the departure from mandates. Departments > administrative reorganization125 retrieves uniform units, decentralization, unpaid/inexperienced officials and changing recruitment; National Assembly > administrative/civil reforms126 retrieves standard local offices. Reform > constitutional/administrative135 and bourgeoisie > Revolutionary role135 retrieve chaotic implementation alongside goodwill and expanded but socially bounded participation. These precise routes preserve every substantive distinction. Full113,116–117,125–127,135 inspected. Departments127 matches only the eligible literal caption topic; it is incidental, unscored and remains a weak unsupported locator, with no map-border/city/annexation claim credited.

Municipal revolution113 retrieves the committees/militias replacing old authority; clergy provincial reactions and municipal revolution114 directly retrieves privileged orders rejection, suspicion and Dijon house arrest. Peasant resistance115 retrieves ineffective inexperienced local militias. Departments125 and municipal revolution126 retrieve replacement of provisional bodies by elected administrations; bourgeoisie135 gives the retrospective participation of propertied groups. These supported topical routes preserve local variation, weak enforcement and restriction to property owners. Final field serialization held solely for corrected113/114 source binding, not uncertain existence of114 candidate access.

Church property132–133 directly retrieves the complete fiscal nationalization dispute: Talleyrand's partial allocation versus Mirabeau's unrestricted national disposal with maintenance obligation, corporate trusteeship versus institutional title and guaranteed property rights, conflicting land-market expectations, and hostile galleries reinforcing prior reform beliefs. Full132–133 read. The unqualified subject heading does not collapse those competing arguments or attribute every proposal to one sponsor. Its133 destination retains the source's November3 vote dating; no outside date correction is substituted. Every principal/supporting treatment and all four retained distinctions are accessible through this focused property route.

Great Fear114 directly retrieves the social/harvest conditions, false conspiracy beliefs, armed mobilization and self-propagating misrecognition. Peasant resistance115 retrieves the related pre-emptive attacks, smoke from burned records and embroidered Quincey reports that amplified panic. Peasantry > Revolution of1789 > Great Fear and rural unrest117 retrieves the calming effect of the August settlement and returning harvest work. Full114–115/117 read. These direct routes preserve rumour versus fact and both retained distinctions without treating an aristocratic brigand army as established or equating later1790 unrest with the original panic.

Necker's financial-management131–132 and popularity131 subentries directly retrieve loss of prestige, failed loans and the inadequate levy. Opposition to nationalization and assignats133–134 retrieves his different bank proposal, Law memories, religious/financial rivalries, later deficit miscalculation and opposition to paper expansion. Recalls and resignations134 independently retrieves the resignation and the eclipse of his methods. Full131–134 read. The valid routes preserve those distinctions and make no claim that public reaction was measured as absent. The unsupported opposition131 posting is excluded; its broader parent financial-management131 is independently supported and retrieves the actual131 claim. No new parent-level loss is inferred merely from that unusable alternative.

Declaration > constitutional role and tensions119 retrieves the free-assent/veto dilemma. October Days121–122 retrieves women initiating the march, subsequent men and Guards, rumours alongside scarcity, palace violence and forced assent; August Decrees > king's refusal121 supplies precise resistance. National Assembly > relocation123 retrieves its later move and recurring metropolitan pressure, independently of the earlier royal transfer122. All scored treatments and retained distinctions are directly accessible through supported routes, so coverage is complete and ordinary event first lookup succeeds. Nevertheless, the separate Louis XVI > relocation to Paris (October Days)112 route conflates the July visit with October confinement; this materially impairs preservation of event chronology and is retained as the same source-linked heading-fit defect already identified for royal authority, rather than a coverage omission. Full119,121–123 inspected;112 also freshly inspected in the linked royal review. Complete treatment recall does not establish complete multi-facet access when the subject's essential stance is only partly preserved.

reader_task_results.rationale: August decrees116–117 retrieves expansion from dues into corporate, provincial and municipal privilege and the destruction of the old principles of organization, answering both treatment and significance.
Active citizens124 supplies eligibility tiers; departments125 the election of judges and territorial administrators, independently of the compensation binding hold.

Municipal revolution113, Great Fear114 and peasant resistance115 retrieve disorder and pressure on deputies. August decrees116–117 supplies response and redemption compromise. Peasant resistance128 and seigneurial rights130 show continuing direct refusal despite legislation. Municipal rejection113/114 binding does not determine this causal question.

Marat and L Ami du Peuple120 retrieve journalists cultivating suspicion and abuse of aristocrat as a label. The separate121 continuation about disliked innocents does not erase this specific task mechanism on120.
Paris government/sections126 retrieve redivision and popular institutional persistence, with Danton126 identifying the local mechanism. No reliance on caption129.
Veto120 retrieves popular hostility, representative compromise and activists insistence on intervention.
Departments125 and municipal revolution126 retrieve electoral territorial reconstruction replacing provisional municipal bodies, beyond their July origins.

Parlements abolition125 and Guard order125–126 retrieve courts without administrative police authority and reliance on unreliable local coercion. Taxation131 retrieves unenforced collection. Together these answer the three causes; separate compensation and deficit page-binding holds do not determine this task.
Municipal revolution113 retrieves committees and militias containing city riot; Foulon and Lafayette command113 supplies Paris lynchings, alarm and failed restraint.
Taxation during the Revolution131 directly retrieves abolition of indirect taxes, monopolies and tax farms, following resistance and preceding replacement assessments.
Royal refusal121 then October Days122 retrieves initial resistance and coerced assent. No credit to the false October royal relocation112 posting.
August decrees117 contrasts redeemed feudal claims with outright tithe abolition; clergy tithes132 gives the consequent state obligation to maintain clergy, predating land nationalization.
Danton126 and Paris sections126 retrieves Cordeliers continuing as Theatre-Francais and local popular institutional persistence.

Paris revolt112 and October Days122 retrieve popular intervention enabling reform. Active citizens124 and Guard martial law126 supply exclusion and legal control. Distinct routes retrieve the whole dependence and restriction tension.

October Days121–122 retrieves bread, suspicion, banquet, women-led action, assent and royal transfer; Assembly relocation123 supplies changed national politics in Paris. Ordinary event access succeeds despite the separate false July112 posting.

John Law133 and Assignats origins133 retrieve memories of1720, hostility to financiers and the rejection of Necker bank proposal in favor of visibly land-backed state claims. Assignats final collapse323 retrieves renewed banking distrust and Lindet campaign defeating the later land bank. Both episodes are directly retrievable; this question does not depend on the separate287 numerical continuation.

Active citizens124 retrieves property-linked political qualifications; bourgeoisie135 gives the wider conclusion that propertied groups participated in municipal government and National Guards. Participation is bounded, not equated with all inhabitants.

Separation of powers119/123 and Constitution1791 features123 retrieves the principle and weak executive arrangement. Parlements abolition125 and Guard order125 retrieves separation stripping courts of administrative functions and leaving enforcement without a new police structure. Direct routes distinguish foundational principle from implementation.

Talleyrand132 retrieves the bishop lending authority to nationalization; Mirabeau financial/ecclesiastical reforms133 retrieves finance grounded on the lands. Church property132 supplies the ownership argument and opposition, keeping the two roles distinct.

Peasant resistance115 retrieves destruction of deeds through forced surrender and burning; seigneurial rights130 retrieves symbols, claims, imposed timetables and intimidation. The routes answer instruments and significance, not just generalized disorder.

Declaration principles118–119 retrieves national sovereignty, natural rights, equality, accountability and separated powers with legal limitations on expression and religion. Active citizens124 exposes political exclusion, property rights132 the Church-nationalization contradiction. All parts of the question and retained facet are reached.

Federation128/135 provides ceremonial participation and apparent unity; Reform135 concludes unprecedented changes still enjoyed wide assent. Full135 also qualifies unanimity with the anti-aristocratic threat in the song and visible exclusions, so the route supports temporary rather than permanent consensus.

Fresh full133–134,323–324,333–334 and384 read. Assignats origins and collapse supply successive monetary forms and exhaustion. Territorial mandates323–324 supply replacement design and demonetization; Directory finance333 supplies subsequent deflation, scarce coin and fiscal strain. Two-Thirds Bankruptcy333–334 supplies default and creditor losses, Agency334 renewed compulsory collection and slow unpopular recovery, Bank of France384 banking, cash debt service and tax improvement with explicitly uncertain foundations. Each phase and limiting qualification in the whole-book question has an actual topic route; no automatic inference from parent completeness.

Declaration principles118–119 provides the actual doctrines and public-order qualifications. Active citizens124 and property rights132 provide contested application to political participation and Church property. Same inspected routes answer this independently stated scope/application question.

Noailles116 and d Aiguillon116 retrieves their different proposals on feudal claims and taxation; Breton Club115 retrieves prior coordination. The source preserves strategy and escalation rather than treating proposals as wholly spontaneous generosity.

Venality116, August decrees117, Parlements abolition and jury125 retrieve institutional abolition and free elected justice; Assignats origins134 compensation enlarging issues. Fresh full408 shows why nominal compensation failed: low declared1771 values preceding later price growth and payment in depreciated paper. Assignats social/professional impact408 and professions408 directly retrieve that different real-value claim. All question components are met; separate bureaucracy409 continuation is not part of this compensation task.
Municipal revolution113 and Guard creation113 retrieve committees organizing citizens militias amid collapse of old authority, with order-maintenance intentions and local variation.

Lafayette command112–113 retrieves appointment, emblem and frustrated control after lynchings. October Days122 supplies pressure by his own guards and protection of royalty; Lafayette command128 retrieves the Federation. These preserve authority and its limits rather than equating title with obedience.
Patriotic Contribution132 retrieves the emergency levy and its failure to solve debt; Assignats origins133 retrieves contribution receipts joining land sales in the Extraordinary Fund.

Paris revolt112 reaches the Bastille governor and Flesselles deaths; Foulon113 the subsequent lynchings; Barnave violence stance113 provides qualified contemporary response. No romanticization of killing is inferred.

Fresh full403 and407–408 read. Assignats decline and National lands403 directly retrieves depressed real sale proceeds. National lands, bourgeoisie gains and property rights407 retrieves enrichment, political dependence on property and demand for guaranteed title; bourgeoisie408 supplies settlement preserved under restored Bourbons. Both independently retained facets ask the same explicit relationship and receive these actual routes. Purchasers gains are not mistaken for universal bourgeois gain or all nobles losing land.

Revolutionary taxation131 retrieves failure of effective collection, reluctance to use force and resistance. Petitioning movement131 supplies organized anti-tax action, distinguishing unwillingness from absence of taxes.

Marat and L Ami du Peuple120 provides radical political journalism and suspicion. Desmoulins124/126 adds persistent democratic criticism and popular organization. This named general press treatment is retrievable independently of one finer121 continuation and the133 source metadata hold.

Federation135 and Reform135 lead directly to the national-consensus conclusion and the contrasting anti-aristocratic threat appended to the optimistic song. The question is about the qualification of unity, not the song as an autonomous musical object.

August decrees117 and venality abolition116 retrieve recognized property and redemption distinctions. Assignats origins134 supplies compensation burden, clergy tithes132 state maintenance, and property rights132 argument over corporate ownership. Combined routes retrieve the reasons for differentiated treatment rather than implying all abolition was confiscation.

Departments, Parlements abolition, cassation and jury125 retrieve administrative and judicial reconstruction. Guard martial law126 supplies the practical dependence on uncertain force, answering the implementation limitation separately from compensation finances.

Constitution1791 features123–124 supplies executive restrictions and electoral tiers; franchise124 and155 retrieves property limits and later revision. Both retained facets ask this same bounded limitation question and are independently covered.

Marat and L Ami du Peuple120 retrieves his journal and cultivating suspicion; Marat134 retrieves political support for assignats displacing financial doubts. Direct named routes cover the specified journalism treatment.

Babeuf131 and petitioning movement131 retrieve his part organizing Picardy resistance and the decline of indirect tax yield. This actual task is on131; the parent broader132 deficit-binding hold is independent.

Paris revolt112 supplies loss of coercive royal authority; refusal121, royal move122 and constitutional role123 retrieve failed resistance, transfer and new constraints enabling reform. These direct paths answer the causal question without relying on the false October move112 entry.

Great Fear114 and peasant resistance115 retrieve starvation and brigand rumours, their weak factual foundation and mobilizing consequence. The routes do not assert the supposed aristocratic plot existed.

Assignats origins133–134 retrieves the Extraordinary Fund combining contribution receipts and land sales, original interest-bearing claims, purchase/retirement mechanism, then currency transformation. The routes preserve successive forms.
October Days121–122 retrieves actual causes, march, royal assent and transfer. No need for the defective royal October relocation112 posting.
Breton Club115 retrieves coordination preceding abolition proposals and d Aiguillon116 retrieves implementation in the session. The strategic connection is explicit.

August decrees116 and Declaration principles118–119 retrieve civil and fiscal equality, while taxation131 supplies practical removal of privilege. Equality is not silently turned into universal voting rights.

Declaration principles118–119 retrieves the enumerated rights and their legal safeguards, with property rights132 retrieving the subsequent conflict over nationalization. The named rights are meaningful explicit claims, not mere mentions.

Monarchiens119/123 retrieves the earlier British-model programme and defeat. Constitution franchise155 and acceptance156–157, with Feuillants158, retrieves later conservative revision and failed legitimacy despite institutional accomplishments. Both retained facets ask this bounded comparison and receive these distinct routes.

Liberty trees130 supplies the explicit coercive planting instrument, and seigneurial rights130 contextualizes villagers demands and threats. Direct named-symbol access answers significance without generic Great Fear chronology.
Church property132–133 and property rights132 retrieves ownership arguments, Declaration guarantee, clerical maintenance and nationalization. Competing interpretations remain visible.

Guard order and martial law126 retrieves distrust of royal/noble officers, desertion and unreliable soldiers as the reason for preferring the Guard, while stating the Guard itself was hard to discipline.
August decrees117 retrieves redemption of property claims; seigneurial rights130 retrieves practical refusal and enforcement weakness. Legal entitlement is distinguished from payment.

Fresh full250,321–322,331,374–375 and409 read, alongside earlier112/126. Guard creation and martial law retrieves citizens militia and limits of civilian coercion. Levee en masse250 retrieves the petition-driven mass mobilization and difference between actual conscription and universal hopes. French Army domestic politics321–322 supplies Vendemiaire replacement of popular coercion and founding military dependence; Fructidor331 supplies army-enforced electoral annulment. Brumaire374–375 retrieves failed chamber persuasion, deception and military clearing enabling regime replacement. Army domestic politics/officer corps409 gives retrospective new careers and generals claiming guardianship. Each stage in the question has its own source-grounded route; success is not derived by merging parent coverage labels.
Guard order125–126 reaches the lack of a new police apparatus, local responsibility, martial-law powers and weak enforcement. It answers the specifically bound administrative public-order question.

Guard provincial138/143/147 retrieves religious division, Jales and effects on soldiers. Lafayette command and Guard order148 retrieves both Day of Daggers and refusal at Saint-Cloud. Varennes151 supplies crisis mobilization, Guard Champ de Mars154 repression. All named settings are separately retrieved, preserving political variation.

Fresh full322–324 and333 read. Assignats collapse322–323 retrieves ruinous depreciation on both payment and revenue sides, failed war rate and specie loan, opposition to a bank and destruction of printing plates. Territorial mandates323–324 retrieves conversion, unrealistic land values, excess issue, speculative purchases, tender withdrawal and formal demonetization. Directory finance333 retrieves scarce specie, debt pressure, falling prices, high interest, barter and fiscal crisis after paper ends. All nine retained facet questions are separately contained in these inspected passages; formal production end, paper demonetization and normal exchange are not conflated.
Great Fear114/117 and peasant resistance115 retrieve rumour, collective mobilization and the legislative response, with the factual weakness of conspiracy claims preserved.
Peasant resistance115 and128 retrieve targeted attacks and the continued selective treatment of rights, rather than generalized indiscriminate violence.

Clergy > provincial reactions and municipal revolution114 directly reaches suspicion of both clergy and nobles, their exclusion from local power and Dijon precautionary arrest. The route is a qualified institutional relation, not an unrelated person on the same page. Source metadata113/114 correction remains pending but the substantive114 access is verified.

Peasant resistance115/128 and seigneurial rights130 retrieve deeds destruction, withholding and direct pressure that continued despite formal law. The routes answer the named action and its legal tension.

Necker financial management131–132, opposition133 and resignation134 retrieves ineffective proposals, defeat over finance and dwindling political authority through resignation. The false opposition131 posting is excluded.

Silver mark155 and Constitution franchise155 directly distinguish abolition of the deputy mark from raising the qualification for secondary electors. The retained facet is covered with the exact contrast, not a general claim that voting became less restrictive.

Guard creation112, martial law126, membership/federation128 and provincial130 retrieves popular origins, political preference over the army, social narrowing, symbolic unity and unreliable rural coercion. It answers all three roles without imposing a single stable allegiance.

Taxation131 retrieves resistance and weak compulsory collection; debt and Assembly finance132 retrieves inherited commitments enlarged by compensation.
